card.name: Rachenitsa
card.tagline: Iconic Bulgarian 7/8 dance, solo or couple, with handkerchief.
card.profile: The iconic Bulgarian dance in 7/8 or 7/16 meter, rhythm 2+2+3 (quick-quick-slow). Performed many ways - solo, in couples, trios, segregated, or in a horo line - most famously as a competitive solo/couple display in which a man and woman try to outdance each other, often waving a handkerchief (the name derives from raka, 'hand'). Widespread across all ethnographic regions, especially Thrace; accompanied by gaida, gadulka, kaval and tapan (Bulgarian folk dance, Wikipedia; Yves Moreau).
card.insight: French scientist Ami Boue described the handkerchief-holding couple dance in the early 19th century; choreographer Boris Tsonev called it 'the crown of all other folk dances' (Folk Dance Federation of California).
card.image_significance: The 7/16 'crown' of Bulgarian dances. A representative image shows folk dress and patterned partner or group figures — Thrace, Bulgaria.
